audit.summary: Supremum-defined Favard spaces are not generally fractional-power domains. A self-adjoint dyadic example refutes Lemma 2.16 and its norm equivalence; the identity is explicitly used in important applications.
limitations: Limitations: No counterexample to every convergence-rate conclusion or to the Coulomb rate was established.
Limitations: No complete repair of general fractional-gamma corollaries was verified.
Limitations: Section 3 is separate and only selectively checked.
False Favard/fractional-domain identification — Counterevidence: D(K^alpha) is continuously included in F_alpha for 0<alpha<1.
False Favard/fractional-domain identification — Counterevidence: For gamma=1, a direct spectral graph-domain commutator estimate yields min(beta,1-alpha) without the false identity.
False Favard/fractional-domain identification — Counterevidence: No counterexample to the paper's Coulomb rate was constructed.
False Favard/fractional-domain identification — Limits: General fractional-gamma results and all multiplier hypotheses not repaired here.
